job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: In class, Ms. Sharma discussed the nature of democracy with Rohan and Meera. Rohan asked, 'Is a country a democracy just because it has a parliament?' Ms. Sharma shook her head, 'Not necessarily. A parliament must be elected through free and fair competition where the ruling party has a real chance of losing.' Meera then asked, 'Does democracy mean the majority can do whatever they want?' Ms. Sharma replied, 'No, that is a common mistake. A true democracy must protect the rights of the minority, even if the majority disagrees. The government is bound by the rule of law and the constitution.' Rohan pondered this and said, 'So, if everyone is allowed to vote, the election is automatically fair?' Ms. Sharma clarified, 'Universal adult franchise is necessary, but not sufficient. For an election to be truly free and fair, there must be a level playing field where opposition parties can campaign without fear or government interference. Democracy is not just about the act of voting or the existence of a legislative body; it is about the limitations placed on power and the protection of individual dignity.'
response.summary: Democracy requires more than just having a parliament or allowing everyone to vote. It is defined by free and fair elections, the rule of law, and the protection of minority rights against the majority.
